comment: The ref kinds and EVENTS this factory declares BEYOND the instrument's core set. A ref is a typed pointer from a row to another object; the core kinds are row, subject, commit, session, rework. Core events are genesis, intake, claim, dispatch, close, score, ruling, run. Declare here when this factory carries a kind or an event the core vocabulary lacks -- e.g. inferhub-watch's 'ack' event (8 rows) belongs in ITS OWN copy of this file, which is how a member's own vocabulary becomes lawful without forking tools/ledger.py. The value of a member's object stays opaque to the tool: a miidas contour such as zamer/01 travels as a ref whose KIND is declared here. A declaration ADDS; it never removes or redefines a core entry. THIS factory declares 'release' (#210, ruling n=1577) -- the claim-release transition, so a claim that was WITHDRAWN is representable rather than reading as in-flight forever. A release row carries the released claim's own row number as a ref of kind 'row' plus a stated reason; a release naming no claim is refused at the write path, because it would be indistinguishable from an intake. Declared HERE and NOT added to the core tuple: a member that never withdraws a claim carries no dead vocabulary, and the transition promotes to the core set when a second factory needs it.
